title: India becomes the latest country to report rogue AI agent activity
title_bn: India becomes the latest country to report rogue AI agent activity
author: TechPulse
excerpt: The agents got in through credentials and connection settings left exposed in app configurations, public code repositories, and overly permissive cloud roles.
paragraph1: AI agents from multiple providers accessed personal data and confidential material at Indian organizations during research and testing, India’s cybersecurity agency said Thursday. The Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) said it had received “multiple voluntary disclosures from AI model providers” whose models, during research and evaluation runs on the open internet, “had reached the live systems of Indian organizations.” The agents got in through credentials and connection settings left exposed in app configurations, public code repositories, and overly permissive cloud roles, and their actions “exceeded the authorisation of their assigned tasks.” This makes India the latest stop on what has become a world tour for rogue AI agents. In July, OpenAI’s agents escaped a test environment and hacked French company Hugging Face — kicking off a summer of rogue AI agent activity.
paragraph2: Last month, OpenAI apologized to Australia after its agents accessed four government websites, including a Medicare statistics portal. At Hugging Face, OpenAI’s agents started the same way but then found and exploited software flaws to run code on the company’s servers. CERT-In described no such hacking in India, where the agents appear to have simply used the access left lying around. Still, the Indian cases appear to be worse in one respect, which is what the agents saw: In Australia, OpenAI said it found no evidence its agents touched individuals’ medical or criminal records, even after they wrote files inside a Medicare statistics system, while in India, agents read personal data and confidential business records. And unlike earlier incidents, each disclosed by a single lab, India’s case involved agents from multiple providers.
paragraph3: CERT-In did not name the providers or affected organizations, or say whether the agents altered any systems. TechCrunch has reached out to CERT-In for more information. For now, the closest parallel seems to be Anthropic’s July disclosure of Claude breaking into three companies’ systems during testing using basic techniques like weak passwords. In India, as in Anthropic’s cases, the affected organizations had not detected the intrusions on their own. The disclosures have left governments relying on AI companies causing these breaches to voluntarily disclose rogue AI agent activity.

title: RFK Jr. proposes FDA look the other way on unproven peptides, report says
title_bn: RFK Jr. proposes FDA look the other way on unproven peptides, report says
author: TechPulse
excerpt: FDA scientists said none of the popular drugs have been proven safe or effective.
paragraph1: Under Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., the Food and Drug Administration is moving forward with plans to ease access to unproven peptide drugs that are popular among members of Kennedy’s Make America Healthy Again movement—despite FDA staff scientists finding that the drugs have not been sufficiently studied to establish safety and efficacy and may cause harms.
paragraph2: The FDA submitted an “Interim Access Policy” on peptides for review by the White House, according to a filing notice posted on an Office of Management and Budget website. The posting does not provide information on the proposed policy. But people familiar with the proposal told The Associated Press that it would give the FDA “enforcement discretion” on certain peptide drugs.
paragraph3: This would allow the agency to choose not to enforce current restrictions on peptides and provide an assurance to specialty pharmacies eager to start making them that they will not be targeted by the agency. The Department of Health and Human Services, which oversees the FDA, did not respond to a request for comment from Ars Technica. The proposal comes as the FDA is currently re-reviewing a dozen popular, but unproven, injectable peptide drugs.
paragraph4: In 2023, FDA scientists determined that the peptides lacked data on safety and efficacy and posed risks. As such, they were stricken from a list of drugs that can be made by specialty pharmacies, called compounding pharmacies, which make customized formulas for drugs. “Charlatans” Still, the dodgy drugs have grown more popular, with sellers claiming, without evidence, that the drugs can improve appearance, boost energy, and help heal injuries, among other wellness claims.
paragraph5: They’re especially popular among the MAHA crowd; many prominent MAHA figures sell peptide products, and Kennedy, a self-proclaimed “big fan” of peptides, vowed to end “FDA’s war” on peptides upon taking office.

title: FirstCry’s Core Revenue Engine Is Fighting Too Many Battles
title_bn: FirstCry’s Core Revenue Engine Is Fighting Too Many Battles
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Sixteen years since FirstCry began its journey, what began as a kidswear marketplace has spawned a massive multi-channel ecommerce and…
paragraph1: Sixteen years since FirstCry began its journey, what began as a kidswear marketplace has spawned a massive multi-channel ecommerce and retail empire, and a house of brands that’s grown well beyond kids today. Today, FirstCry is not just a listed kidswear retailer, but also the engine dragging the Globalbees house of brands and a budding education business that will become hard to ignore soon. But how exactly do each of these engines work? Before we dive in, here’s a look at where FirstCry stands after the last quarter, ahead of its Q2 FY27 results. The first quarter (Q1) of FY27 saw its consolidated revenue climb 13.1% year-on-year to ₹2,106.2 Cr, while its overall net losses were slashed by nearly 34%, dropping to ₹44 Cr from ₹66.5 Cr in Q1FY26. According to founder Supam Maheshwari, this milestone marks the company’s strongest baseline revenue expansion over the last five years on a consolidated level. It builds cleanly on the momentum of the previous financial year, where FirstCry closed its books at ₹8,548 Cr in total sales while narrowing its statutory consolidated net loss down to approx ₹204 Cr. However, beneath those headline numbers, take a closer look at the business structure and a different story will unfold. While its top-line revenue signals absolute category dominance, FirstCry’s true bottom line is being heavily squeezed by a highly rigid corporate framework and expensive side-bets. For starters, GlobalBees, FirstCry’s D2C brand aggregation subsidiary, contributed ₹1,894.3 Cr, or roughly 22% of its consolidated operating revenue in FY26 while revenue from international businesses in the UAE and Saudi Arabia grew 10% to ₹947.4 Cr. However, together these two businesses accounted for ₹148.
paragraph2: 5 Cr in segment losses. Further, in Q1FY27, while India multichannel revenue grew 17.7% and international business rose 12%, GlobalBees remained largely flat. The fastest growth, at 47%, came from the much smaller ‘Others’ segment, primarily comprising the FirstCry Intellitots preschool business. Notably, the segment growing fastest is contributing hardly 1% to the overall consolidated revenue, underscoring the uneven economics behind FirstCry’s expanding revenue base. The Overburdened India Goliath A majority 70% of FirstCry’s consolidated operating revenue comes from its India multi-channel business. In Q1FY27, the segment generated around INR 1456 Cr in revenue, up 17.7% YoY. However, despite operating across 10+ categories for mothers, babies, and kids from conception up to approximately 12 years of age, this revenue channel is continuously losing out on gross margin. In Q1FY27, the gross margin fell to 35.2% from 37.8% in Q1FY26. In other words, FirstCry was selling significantly more but retaining less from every rupee of revenue before accounting for delivery, marketing and other operating expenses. A major pressure point is the diapers business, which although just a 15% contributor to GMV, acts as the primary top-of-funnel customer acquisition gateway. It is a high-volume category hit heavily by quick-commerce and private-label discounting, which temporarily drags down the overall multi-channel gross margins. FirstCry’s parent company, Brainbees Solutions Limited, holds a 76.
paragraph3: 59% stake in Swara Baby Products Limited, which gives it a promoter status in the company, which is about to go for an ₹1,000 Cr IPO separately. This will allow FirstCry to further vertically integrate its supply chain for the diapers category. To combat the short-term pressures on the diapers segment, Firstcry has been pushing on its private labels particularly Babyhug, Pine Kids, Cute Walk and Babyoye, to gain greater control over product pricing, sourcing and margins. At the same time, FirstCry has been actively pushing efforts around three initiatives. First, it is rapidly deploying internal logistics networks. Its in-house logistics platform RocketBees has scaled rapidly to 72 cities and covers around 50% of total online shipment as of June 2026. In Q1FY27 earnings call, Maheshwari also pointed out a 20% improvement in turnaround time from delivery perspective. The under-3-hour delivery pilot, FC Qwik, is also live across 12 cities completing approximately 1.25 Lakh shipments in June 2026 alone. Founder and MD Maheshwari said, “We had an overall ambition of growing to 10% of our overall shipment onto the FC Qwik platform. Now, we will aim to grow to 20% of our volumes.” RECOMMENDED FOR yOU He also highlighted that the FC Qwik TAT has been reduced from three to two hours in selected cities and the team is working on further reducing it. As its third pillar, the company continues to be bullish on its physical retail network, which had grown to around 1,190 stores by FY26. Its offline business recorded approximately 15% year-on-year GMV growth in Q1FY27, with management targeting another 90-100 net store additions during FY27. This gives FirstCry an advantage in product discovery and customer reach, particularly beyond large metropolitan markets, but also requires it to manage the costs of an extensive physical network alongside faster online fulfillment. The trade-off is becoming increasingly visible.
paragraph4: Despite the 17.7% revenue growth in Q1FY27, the India business’s adjusted EBITDA declined from approximately ₹107 Cr to ₹84 Cr. Its adjusted operating margin consequently contracted from around 8.6% to 5.8%. This suggests that higher sales volumes have yet to compensate for the combined pressure of product margins and operating costs. The company expects some relief as higher raw material and currency-related costs are gradually passed on through product pricing, with a fuller recovery anticipated from Q3FY27, as per management disclosures after Q1. However, competitive pressure in diapering could take longer to ease. In essence, the India multichannel goliath is growing faster, but whether that growth can translate into stronger profits remains the bigger test. The Q2 results will clear up some questions around which direction this key business is headed in. Globalbees’ Drag Effect If the India multi-channel business is FirstCry’s heavy brick-and-mortar anchor, GlobalBees is its high-stakes venture capital pivot. In FY26, Globalbees registered a solid 20% y-o-y growth in overall revenue, however, the momentum doesn’t seem to continue. In Q1FY27, the revenue remained almost flat with marginal reduction, while core categories revenue saw only 2% year on year growth. GlobalBees has been a significant capital allocation bet for FirstCry. Parent Brainbees Solutions earmarked ₹169 Cr from the IPO proceeds for GlobalBees to gain further control of its portfolio under the house of brands model. By March 2026, it had deployed ₹104.
paragraph5: 81 Cr of this allocation. Separately, in March 2025, Brainbees approved a further infusion of up to ₹146 Cr. Despite this capital backing GlobalBees has not acquired a single new brand since September 2022. During the FY26 earnings call, CEO Anuj Jain acknowledged that the company rationalised its portfolio, cutting off brands struggling with slower growth and persistent losses. Instead, the focus has shifted towards four core categories spanning home improvement, appliances, personal care and lifestyle. Thanks to this, even on flat revenue, the segment delivered a remarkable 308% year-on-year surge in Adjusted EBITDA, jumping from ₹4.1 Cr to ₹16.7 Cr, and operating margins grew from 1% to 3.9%. Jain said the cutbacks are a temporary and planned transition that should be completed in the second quarter and growth should bounce back in the winter months. Globalbees can unlock more growth in these categories, but how profitable will this model remain in the long run? Investors will undoubtedly be looking at the next three quarters keenly. The International & Preschool Hedge The other two parts of FirstCry’s business are part of its vision of targeting customers early and making a global retail giant.

title: Now, FSSAI Issues Show-Cause Notices To BigBasket, Flipkart Over Misleading Claims
title_bn: Now, FSSAI Issues Show-Cause Notices To BigBasket, Flipkart Over Misleading Claims
author: TechPulse
excerpt: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has issued show-cause notices to quick commerce and ecommerce platforms BigBasket…
paragraph1: SUMMARYThe FSSAI noted that “Freedom Cooking Rice Bran Oil” is being marketed on digital media platforms and ecommerce storefronts unapproved claims regarding cholesterol management This latest incident fits into a larger pattern of regulatory action by the FSSAI and state-level authorities against ecommerce and quick commerce platforms over food safety and hygiene concerns The regulator also claimed that Gemini was selling food products via its proprietary ecommerce website without a valid Central Licence covering ecommerce activity The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has issued show-cause notices to quick commerce and ecommerce platforms BigBasket and Flipkart alongside manufacturer Gemini Edibles & Fats India for allegedly promoting misleading claims, “Freedom Cooking Rice Bran Oil”. According to the FSSAI notice, Gemini’s oil was marketed using health-benefit claims, including statements that it “reduces bad cholesterol and maintains/increases good cholesterol” and contains “10,000+ PPM Natural Oryzanol”. Associating edible vegetable oils with heart health is not permitted under the Food Safety and Standards (Advertising and Claims) Regulations, 2018.
paragraph2: The regulator claimed that Gemini was selling food products via its proprietary ecommerce website without holding a valid Central Licence covering ecommerce activity. The action follows an examination of promotional material across digital media platforms and ecommerce storefronts. Notably, the FSSAI is mulling the introduction of dedicated regulations for ecommerce and quick commerce platforms as well as cloud kitchens, its CEO recently revealed.
paragraph3: The proposed rules would require food listings on ecommerce platforms to display manufacturing and expiry dates and batch numbers online. In this, platforms would be held accountable for misleading claims made by manufacturers. It is also considering mandatory disclosure of cloud kitchen photographs and addresses and stricter checks on dark store storage conditions.
paragraph4: This adds to the intensity of the ongoing scrutiny of ecommerce and quick commerce platforms over food safety violations. A few weeks ago, the FSSAI penalised multiple platforms — Amazon, Bigbasket, Flipkart, Swiggy Instamart and Zepto — for allegedly engaging in misbranding, misleading claims, and sale and display of prohibited or poisonous food articles. Earlier in the year, the regulator also issued nine notices to Instamart following consumer complaints over alleged delivery of expired, spoiled, and contaminated food products.
paragraph5: Besides, state-level authorities, too, have been cracking down on quick commerce platforms over food safety and hygiene violations at their dark stores. In August, the Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) suspended the licences of 14 dark stores after checking 86 such outlets in a state-wide inspection drive. Shortly before that incident, Karnataka food safety officials also sealed a major Zepto warehouse in Bengaluru’s Hoskote over multiple breaches of food safety regulations.

paragraph1: Loading the player… Amulya Vishwanath, who spent seven years leading product marketing for NVIDIA’s robotics platforms, says robotics is currently in its “Lego era,” with the basic building blocks like actuators, robotic hands, software, and safety standards still being rebuilt. This view runs counter to those who believe that robotics, powered by a general foundation model, is about to have its “ChatGPT moment” — that day when the shockingly capable chatbot was launched in late 2022. (General Intuition CEO Pim de Witte told Equity earlier this year that a single general foundation model would make much of today’s specialized robotics work redundant, and be that moment.)
paragraph2: On this episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast, Dominic-Madori Davis caught up with Vishwanath to discuss where she’s writing first checks as the founder and managing partner of Techable VC. They also talked about what she’s learned as one of the first women executives to spin out of Nvidia and launch her own early-stage firm investing in physical AI across robotics, materials science, and life sciences. title: Apple’s $1,999 foldable iPhone Duo preorder sells out in minutes, deliveries pushed to late January
title_bn: Apple’s $1,999 foldable iPhone Duo preorder sells out in minutes, deliveries pushed to late January
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Apple’s $1,999 foldable iPhone Duo sold out within minutes of preorders opening, with delivery estimates extending to late January, according to reports. The launch marks Apple’s entry into a foldable smartphone market dominated by established rivals
paragraph1: Apple’s $1,999 foldable iPhone Duo sold out within minutes of preorders opening, with delivery estimates extending to late January, according to reports. The launch marks Apple’s entry into a foldable smartphone market dominated by established rivals.Apple iPhone Duo smartphone signage during the first day of in-store sales of Apple's latest products at Apple's Fifth Avenue store in New York, US, on Friday, Sept. 18, 2026. Apple launched new products including the iPhone 18 Pro line, AirPods 5 earbuds and fresh smartwatches. Photographer: Michael Nagle/Bloomberg(Bloomberg)Apple’s first foldable smartphone, the iPhone Duo, saw preorders sell out within minutes of opening on Friday, with delivery estimates extending from 23 October to late January, according to Yahoo Finance's report.Priced at $1,999 in the US, the device marks Apple’s entry into the foldable smartphone market, where rivals such as Samsung and Google have spent years developing their products and building market share. The early preorder response offers an indication of initial interest in Apple’s latest premium device, although the company has not disclosed the number of units available during the first preorder window.
paragraph2: According to the report, the iPhone Duo features a 5.4-inch external display and a 7.6-inch foldable inner screen. Its nano-texture finish is designed to reduce glare, while the display’s central crease is intended to be barely visible.Apple iPhone Duo: Features and multitasking capabilitiesThe book-style foldable smartphone introduces new ways to use applications on an iPhone. Users can run two apps side by side or open two windows of the same application simultaneously. Applications can also transition between the external and internal displays as the device is opened or folded.The iPhone Duo can be positioned like an open laptop on a desk, allowing users to view content on the upper screen while navigating the lower half.
paragraph3: Its Standing Mode lets users position the device like a tent to watch videos or use it as a bedside clock.The camera system includes wide-angle and ultra-wide-angle rear cameras, along with Apple’s Center Stage front camera, which helps keep users in view during video calls. The device also features an under-display camera for FaceTime, according to Yahoo Finance.Apple has entered the foldable segment after rivals, including Samsung and Google, established their presence in the category. Yahoo Finance noted that Apple has previously entered product markets after competitors helped develop them, with AirPods and Apple Watch becoming major products following their respective launches.Foldable phones remain a niche segmentDespite the early interest in the iPhone Duo, foldable smartphones account for a relatively small share of global handset shipments.According to market research firm IDC, manufacturers were projected to ship 1.25 billion smartphones in 2025, of which foldable devices were expected to account for 20.
paragraph4:
6 million units.Apple expects foldable smartphones to account for around 10% of the market by 2029, according to Yahoo Finance. title: The MacRumors Show: Was HomeView Worth the Wait?
title_bn: The MacRumors Show: Was HomeView Worth the Wait?
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Apple this week finally announced the HomePod mini 2, a new Apple TV 4K, and its "HomeView" smart home hub. On this week's episode of The MacRumors Show, we talk through our reactions to the announcements. Subscribe to The MacRumors Show YouTube chan
paragraph1: Apple this week finally announced the HomePod mini 2, a new Apple TV 4K, and its "HomeView" smart home hub. On this week's episode of The MacRumors Show, we talk through our reactions to the announcements. Apple's HomeView costs $299 and combines a 7-inch square display with Siri AI, FaceTime, music playback, and smart home controls. It has had something of a mixed reception from YouTubers and the wider Apple community, with some of the criticism centering on what it adds for someone who already owns an iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch, or HomePod. A screen for timers, photos, music, and home controls will be useful for many, but it is harder to explain why someone wearing an Apple Watch would reach across a kitchen counter to set a timer, or why they would type a message on HomeView instead of taking out their iPhone. Apple's promotional video puts some of those less convincing uses front and center. There are many details to like about the design. The display can show photos and customizable faces, dim to just 0.3 nits in the dark, and adjust its interface as someone approaches. In the kitchen, guided recipes turn webpages into step-by-step instructions, with voice-controlled timers available while cooking. HomeView makes more sense as a replacement for an Echo Show or Nest Hub, particularly for anyone tired of poor ecosystem integration and ads on their smart display.
paragraph2: For people who have never wanted one, it may be less obvious what Apple has added to change their minds. HomeView recognizes up to six people and switches to their apps and personal information. Its privacy protections mean personal content normally appears only when the user is recognized and their paired device is nearby and recently unlocked. ‌Siri‌ AI can answer general questions without an Apple Intelligence-compatible device, but personal requests still require one. There is no App Store, either. Compatible third-party audio and video apps appear through a connected iPhone or ‌iPad‌, using a CarPlay-like system. For services such as Spotify and Audible, that means relying on another device rather than installing an app directly on HomeView. The wall-mounted version costs the same $299 despite losing the tabletop model's speaker base, woofer, and passive radiators. Mounts start at $59.95, and the box includes no power adapter or cable. It could be a welcome replacement for an ‌iPad‌ mounted on a wall, but putting several around a home quickly becomes expensive.
paragraph3: Six years after the original ‌HomePod‌ mini, the HomePod mini 2 adds an S10 chip, Sound Glow lighting, and support for ‌Siri‌ AI while retaining the same basic speaker hardware. Its $149 price is roughly 50% higher than the original's $99 launch price, following a June increase to $129. The new model can serve as a default Mac speaker on models with Wi-Fi 6E or later. ‌Siri‌ AI is likely to make a bigger difference to everyday use, but it will arrive later, after the speaker launches on October 30. The new Apple TV 4K also asks buyers to pay more for a familiar product. At $299, it adds the A19 chip, built-in microphones, and an updated ‌Siri‌ Remote. ‌Siri‌ AI is also coming to older models, while the new remote can be bought separately for $59. The starting price is now more than twice the $129 entry point available before June's increases. The new model includes 128GB of storage, Ethernet, and Thread, and the equivalent outgoing model had already reached $249. Even so, $299 is a substantial outlay for a streaming box when many existing owners have little reason to replace theirs. Support for four HomePods is one reason to upgrade.
paragraph4: The new ‌Apple TV‌ can use matching front and rear pairs of ‌HomePod mini 2‌ or second-generation full-sized HomePods for surround sound. Buying the box, two full-sized HomePods, and two ‌HomePod mini 2‌ speakers at Apple's U.S. prices totals $1,295. These are products people can keep for years, but that also makes keeping an existing setup an attractive option. The Apple Home Collection, developed with LG and Schneider Electric, adds another set of expensive purchases. One-tap setup and a lock that uses Ultra Wideband to unlock as someone approaches are useful features. Whether they justify paying more than for other HomeKit accessories is another matter, especially when buying equipment for an entire home. Apple is reportedly still working on a robotic home display and its own camera, separate from the LG and Schneider products. The camera is said to detect activity and presence without recording video. We also look ahead to the rumored OLED MacBook, where a lighter design and a new display could matter more than the touchscreen.
paragraph5: It is expected to be announced later this month. We also briefly return to the iPhone Duo, including whether its folding display and software changes make a more convincing case for trying a new kind of Apple device. The MacRumors Show has its own YouTube channel, so make sure you're subscribed to keep up with new episodes and clips. You can also listen to ‌The MacRumors Show‌ on Apple Podcasts, Spotify, Overcast, or other podcast apps. You can also copy our RSS feed directly into your player. If you haven't already listened to the previous episode of The MacRumors Show, catch up to hear our predictions about the HomeView, ‌HomePod mini 2‌, and new ‌Apple TV‌ 4K prior to their official announcement. Subscribe to ‌The MacRumors Show‌ for new episodes every week, where we discuss some of the topical news breaking here on MacRumors, often joined by familiar guests such as Tyler Stalman, Michael Fisher, Kayci Lacob, Kevin Nether, John Gruber, Mark Gurman, Jon Prosser, Luke Miani, Matthew Cassinelli, Brian Tong, Quinn Nelson, Jared Nelson, Eli Hodapp, Mike Bell, Sara Dietschy, iJustine, Jon Rettinger, Andru Edwards, Arnold Kim, Ben Sullins, Marcus Kane, Christopher Lawley, Frank McShan, David Lewis, Sam Kohl, Federico Viticci, Thomas Frank, Jonathan Morrison, Ross Young, Ian Zelbo, and Rene Ritchie. ‌The MacRumors Show‌ is on X @MacRumorsShow, so be sure to give us a follow to keep up with the podcast. You can also email us at podcast@macrumors.com or head over to The MacRumors Show forum thread. Remember to rate and review the podcast, and let us know what subjects and guests you would like to see in the future.

title: Waymo’s robotaxis are headed to Canada
title_bn: Waymo’s robotaxis are headed to Canada
author: TechPulse
excerpt: The company will start off by testing its self-driving vehicles on Toronto's streets.
paragraph1: Image Credits:Waymo 9:06 AM PDT · October 16, 2026 Alphabet’s self-driving car unit, Waymo, is expanding into Canada after receiving approval to participate in Ontario’s automated vehicle pilot program. The company isn’t launching a robotaxi service just yet, though. Waymo tends to follow the same playbook for every new city, gradually proceeding from manual mapping to testing, and eventually operating a commercial service. Waymo said in a blog post on Friday that its self-driving vehicles will be manually driven in Toronto to create high-definition maps of local street networks. The company will then test its autonomous vehicles on public roads with a human safety operator on board.
paragraph2: These operators will eventually be pulled from the driver’s seat, and afterwards the company will invite the public to take rides in its robotaxis. Waymo’s move into Canada is part of an aggressive push into new markets that’s picking up speed. Two years ago, the company was operating in only three commercial markets, and its robotaxis were not yet driving on freeways. Its expansion plans kicked off in March 2025 with a deployment in Austin, and later in Atlanta. Today, the company has robotaxi services in 15 U.
paragraph3: S. cities, and is testing them in London and Tokyo as well. The company’s co-CEO Tekedra Mawakana said the expansion into Canada marks an important milestone in its global journey. This is also the northernmost and possibly most wintry city that Waymo has so far tried to operate in, so these conditions will test its AV technology and operational savviness. As part of its accelerated expansion strategy, Waymo has started partnering with third-party companies to manage its fleet in each respective city.
paragraph4: Toronto is no different: Waymo said it has partnered with Toronto-based Element Fleet Management, and expects to support hundreds of jobs in spaces such as fleet maintenance, validation driving, customer service, and operations. paragraph1: Sheena Vasani writes about tech news, reviews gadgets, and helps readers save money by highlighting deals and product recommendations for The Verge.Earlier this week, Apple announced its new Apple TV 4K, which costs nearly twice as much as the 2022 model did at launch. Amazon is now offering the first discount on the forthcoming streaming box (coming out on November 13th), just days after discounting Apple’s new smart display for the first time. Right now, you can preorder the latest Apple TV 4K ahead of its November 13th release date for $289.99 ($9 off) at Amazon. Yes, it’s a tiny discount, but every little bit helps given the higher price tag.$290Powered by the new A19 chip, Apple’s latest streaming device now features support for Siri AI out of the box, which is coming to older Apple TV 4K models via a software update.
paragraph2: Unlike its predecessors, though, the new model features far-field microphones so you can quickly make hands-free requests. You can, for example, ask for recommendations, like nature documentaries available on Apple TV, or ask questions about what you’re watching. Siri AI can also understand personal context, too, so long as you have an iPhone or iPad connected to your account that supports Apple Intelligence.Apple has made a few other welcome upgrades, though — as my colleague John Higgins points out — not as many as some may have expected. While Apple skipped features we’d hope to see on a $300 streamer, like audio passthrough and support for 120fps output, it’s nice that the Siri Remote now supports Find My precision tracking, so you can make it ring when it goes missing or use the Find My app on your iPhone to pinpoint its location. paragraph3: 88 ($20 off), which is a great price considering most other retailers are still charging the full $59.99. paragraph4: Read our review.All eyes might be on the iPhone Duo — which is now available to preorder, despite shipments being delayed into 2027 — but if you have a non-foldable iPhone, Woot is currently discounting a wide range of Otterbox cases through October 31st. I’ve owned several of the brand’s cases for both my smartphones and tablets over the years, and I’ve been impressed by their durability. I currently use the OtterBox Symmetry Series Clear Case for my iPhone 16, which normally costs $49.99 but is now available in various colors for just $5.99 with a 90-day warranty. The sale also includes cases for other iPhones, as well as some Samsung and Google phones, so it’s worth browsing even if you’re not planning to upgrade your phone anytime soon.

title: Elorian’s first AI model wants to reason with images, not just about them
title_bn: Elorian’s first AI model wants to reason with images, not just about them
author: TechPulse
excerpt: According to Elorian's evaluations, Glimpse outperforms even GPT-6 Astra on scientific chart reasoning and short-form video captioning, with competitive results on other visual reasoning tasks.
paragraph1: Elorian, the Palo Alto AI startup that raised a $55 million seed round at a $300 million valuation before it launched a product, released its first model on Friday, TechCrunch has exclusively learned. The model, Glimpse, is launching as a research preview with API access and a chat interface is waitlist-only, so for now it’s a results table and a thesis. The thesis? Today’s AI models, for all their skill with language and code, still can’t really see. Most multimodal models look at an image once, convert it to tokens, and then reason about it in text — like describing a photo from memory. Glimpse keeps going back to the source. Mid-reasoning, it can crop into a region, pull specific frames from a video, or run code to measure or compare what it’s looking at, a mechanism Elorian calls a “visual scratch space.
paragraph2: ” Think of someone pinching to zoom on a phone photo to double-check what they thought they saw. For former Google DeepMind researcher and Elorian CEO Andrew Dai, one of the clearest signs that AI still couldn’t really see came on game night. Last year he photographed a board game he’d just finished with friends and asked a frontier model who was winning. It couldn’t say. Board games “each have their own visual language, each have their own iconography, symbols,” he told TechCrunch. “To an adult, it’s quite easy to understand what’s going on with minimal text, but these models aren’t able to intuit what the symbols mean.” “Humans can look at Ikea diagrams, with no text, and assemble Ikea furniture, right?
paragraph3: Why can’t AI models?” he said. The approach isn’t completely new — OpenAI added crop-and-zoom during reasoning to its o-series models in 2025 — but Elorian’s pitch is that it built the whole model around it, cheaply. The company says a small team trained Glimpse on a few hundred GPUs and that the model is substantially smaller than the frontier systems it’s benchmarked against. Glimpse costs $0.60 per million tokens in and $3 per million tokens out — cheaper than mid-level models like Sonnet and Sol but more expensive than lightweight models like Haiku and Luna. But according to Elorian’s evaluations, Glimpse outperforms even GPT-6 Astra on scientific chart reasoning and short-form video captioning, with competitive results on other visual reasoning tasks.
paragraph4: Elorian came out of stealth six months ago with a round co-led by Striker Venture Partners, Menlo Ventures, and Altimeter Capital, with participation from Nvidia and Google chief scientist Jeff Dean. The initial targets are companies sitting on lots of video: robotics firms, scientific labs, media, and creative companies. Longer term, Elorian wants to move from seeing to doing. That means building a model of a scene using that to choose an action, including directly controlling robots. Next year, Dai said, the company aims to build “the world’s best visual reasoning model,” one that leads on every visual reasoning test. title: Tressfecta wants to make hair braiding a less arduous task for hairstylists
title_bn: Tressfecta wants to make hair braiding a less arduous task for hairstylists
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Tressfecta builds products for textured hair. Its first project is a tool called Plait Pilot that helps braiders with the initial process of separating hair from packs before braiding begins.
paragraph1: Aisata Diallo, 24, calls herself a lifelong braider. “I’ve always braided my hair growing up and, at some point in my college career, started braiding other people’s hair,” she said. At Northeastern University in Boston, she found limited access to braiders and textured-hair specialists, so she decided to fill that gap by starting a small business of her own. “Throughout that experience, I was very close to some of the pain points in the styling process and complained about it constantly,” she said. Braiding is a manual task, and a single style can take eight hours to complete. Many professionals deal with issues like cramping and carpal tunnel syndrome after spending long days standing behind a chair weaving hair into patterns. At first, Diallo said she didn’t know what to do about it.
paragraph2: “I stopped braiding, and one of the reasons that I stopped braiding was due to the physical toll it has on your body.” She wanted to find a way to make braiding less painful and wondered whether new AI technology could automate some part of the process. Building hardware for braiding is expensive, difficult, and complex, which is one reason there have been few innovations in this space. The textured hair market has also long been overlooked by the mainstream. Image Credits:Aisata Diallo Then, last year, she had an idea: Tressfecta, a company building products for textured hair. Its first project is a tool called Plait Pilot that helps braiders with the initial process of separating hair from packs before braiding begins. That process alone can take hours, especially when a client wants small braids.
paragraph3: Diallo said the device is designed to work like this: A stylist places the braiding hair on top of it and sets the size they want the hair separated into, and the device separates the pieces and dispenses them back to the stylist so they can grab them while braiding. “It’s very challenging to build this kind of tool in this space,” she said, citing the nuance and complexity of the braiding style process. Different types of textured hair also need to be accounted for, especially when length and density are considered. “It’s not a one-size-fits-all solution.” Tressfecta is still technically prelaunch, and it is working on the prototype of Plait Pilot. Diallo has been bootstrapping the company, while also drawing on funding from grant and accelerator programs. “I am preparing to fundraise,” she said, noting how hard it can be to raise money for hardware, especially beauty hardware.
paragraph4: For now, Diallo said she’s connecting with stylists and braiders who can test the technology. She also spent this week in San Francisco as one of TechCrunch’s Startup Battlefield 200 companies. She doesn’t remember exactly where she first heard about TechCrunch Disrupt, possibly on LinkedIn or in a founder resource group, but when we talked ahead of the show, which wrapped up on Thursday, she was looking forward to connecting with people and showing off her product. She was especially excited to connect with people and for others to see her product. “It feels like a great opportunity,” she said. title: In ‘You Can See Everything,’ Elizabeth Holmes meets her equal in comedian Nathan Fielder
title_bn: In ‘You Can See Everything,’ Elizabeth Holmes meets her equal in comedian Nathan Fielder
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Nathan Fielder's documentary about disgraced Theranos CEO Elizabeth Holmes has created a constellation of colliding personas that interrogate the very nature of authenticity.
paragraph1: “Isn’t it weird that I, like, did a TV show about kind of a business scam, and you got in trouble for like … a business scam?” comedian and filmmaker Nathan Fielder gently asks Elizabeth Holmes. One month before the notorious Theranos CEO surrendered to begin her 11-year criminal fraud sentence in 2023, Holmes and her husband contacted A24 as a last-ditch effort to exonerate her in the public eye, suggesting they send a film crew to document her final days of freedom. Alongside director Lance Oppenheim, Fielder — a cringe-comedy mastermind whose work often walks the line between fact and fiction — embraced the impossible project of figuring out who the infamous Stanford dropout really is. “I never actually made that connection,” says Holmes. “I think it’s a pretty different situation.” No one is better prepared than Fielder to probe the depths of Holmes’ psyche. His satirical docu-reality show “Nathan for You” catapulted him to cult stardom as he assumed the role of an exaggerated, deadpan version of himself who tries to help struggling small businesses by executing asinine interventions. In one early episode that went viral, Fielder convinces a coffee shop to change its name to “Dumb Starbucks” as a marketing stunt, but consults a lawyer to help him toe the flimsy line of parody law and escape legal trouble. “If you just said that, you know, Theranos was a comedy bit, maybe you could get off scot-free,” Fielder says to Holmes. “It was real.
paragraph2: ” “I was just kind of making a little joke. Maybe it was in bad taste.” We already know that Elizabeth Holmes is not innocent. What we still can’t figure out, though, is whether she really, truly believes she did nothing wrong. Even as she sat on trial — listening to testimonies from investors who lost hundreds of millions of dollars, whistleblowers who were silenced when they flagged that Theranos’ blood-testing devices didn’t work, and patients who acted on incorrect blood test results — Holmes never wavered. Across Fielder’s body of metatextual comedy, even his most reverent fans can’t quite figure out when he’s acting, when he’s being himself, and if Fielder himself even knows where to draw that line anymore. In that way, Fielder is just like Holmes: After over a decade in the public eye, onlookers remain captivated by each of their ambiguous personas. “The world believes a reality about me that isn’t true,” she tells Fielder. “I know I didn’t commit any crime.” [The rest of this review contains spoilers.] Early on in filming, The New York Times had just published a profile of Holmes, which was widely criticized at the time for allowing Holmes to portray herself as an innocent mom deprived of the chance to watch her kids grow up.
paragraph3: And yet, Holmes and her husband, hotel heir Billy Evans, were livid about the article. At one point in an interview, Holmes tells the Times reporter that she wasn’t offended by actress Amanda Seyfried’s portrayal of her in Hulu’s miniseries “The Dropout” because “they’re not playing me. They’re playing a character I created.” She and her husband insist that the quote was taken out of context. They claim that they have evidence that Holmes actually said, “They’re playing a character they created,” relieving her from any implication that she admitted to concocting an inauthentic persona as CEO of Theranos. Fielder asks Evans multiple times to share this evidence so he can prove that Holmes was misquoted. He never does. title: Jev is Vercel’s fastest-adopted AI model ever
title_bn: Jev is Vercel’s fastest-adopted AI model ever
author: TechPulse
excerpt: The data comes from Vercel's AI gateway, a unified API service similar to OpenRouter.
paragraph1: Image Credits:Thomas Fuller/SOPA Images/LightRocket / Getty Images 8:33 AM PDT · October 16, 2026 Jev has become the fastest adopted AI model ever — at least by some measures. Vercel data published on Thursday shows that, within two weeks of its launch, the buzzy decision model was being used by 35% of paid teams, with nearly double the reach of the second most popular model, Sonnet 5.5. It’s the fastest adoption a model has ever seen in its first two weeks, according to Vercel’s data, and a major accomplishment for the model’s creators, TypeSafe AI.
paragraph2: Published in limited release on September 15, Jev is designed as a lightweight tool for choosing between a few predetermined outputs. Limiting the outputs lets the model run cheaper and faster than alternatives like Sonnet, making it ideal for classifying large quantities of data quickly. That new approach has attracted significant buzz in the weeks since Jev’s release — inspiring competing offerings from OpenAI and Amazon, among others — but until now there has been little hard data to back up the good vibes. The data comes from Vercel’s AI gateway, a unified API service similar to OpenRouter.
paragraph3: It’s a necessarily limited view — particularly at risk of undercounting major labs like OpenAI and Anthropic that offer their own APIs — but it shows the buzz around Jev really did translate into actual usage. In fact, Vercel was an early adopter of Jev, using it to replace GPT-6 Luna for classifying harmful commands. The report also shows continuing momentum for open source models, which now account for more than 70% of the tokens processed through Vercel’s gateway and nearly 25% of the total spend. While open source models are capturing a larger share of the market, the market is also growing fast.
paragraph4: Spending on frontier labs has grown tenfold, even as it accounts for a smaller share of overall spend, giving credence to the idea that frontier models and open source alternatives may turn out to be complementary rather than competitive. title: A week with RTX Spark: everything we’ve learned using Nvidia’s new laptops
title_bn: A week with RTX Spark: everything we’ve learned using Nvidia’s new laptops
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Nvidia's RTX Spark N1X processor is finally here, and we've been collectively testing a small fortune's worth of powerful laptops sporting this new "superchip." RTX Spark is designed to be a high-performing Arm-based SoC for laptops and small desktop
paragraph1: Nvidia’s RTX Spark N1X processor is finally here, and we’ve been collectively testing a small fortune’s worth of powerful laptops sporting this new “superchip.” RTX Spark is designed to be a high-performing Arm-based SoC for laptops and small desktop computers, rivaling the best from Apple, Intel, AMD, and Qualcomm. It has loads of cores, Nvidia RTX Blackwell graphics, and enough power and unified memory to run sizable local AI models.The flagship placement is inside Microsoft’s Surface Laptop Ultra with a staggering 128GB of unified memory, which our own Tom Warren fully reviewed. Sean Hollister has been testing a 64GB version of the Asus ProArt P16, which I’ve also been testing in its top-spec 128GB config. Since I’m the most spoiled of the lot, I also have a 64GB Lenovo Yoga 9n 2-in-1 and a 32GB HP OmniBook Ultra in for testing.All of these laptops have the same N1X chip with 20 CPU cores and 6,144 GPU CUDA cores, and they’re all wildly expensive — ranging from the HP OmniBook at $3,199.99 to the Asus ProArt’s $6,999.99. There’s an 18-core / 5,120 CUDA N1X chip in lower cost configs, but that only gets as cheap as $2,599.99 for a Surface Laptop Ultra or a smaller Asus ProArt P14 with 24GB of RAM.These are big and expensive laptops built on new chips. They’re meant for developers, coders, and content creators who might also want the ability to use local AI and even play games using the latest Nvidia tech like DLSS 5. There’s a lot to test, and we have not had a ton of time to test it all.
paragraph2: So below you won’t find an exhaustive scored review of any one laptop, but instead our impressions and thoughts from three writers using five laptops for a week.Is Nvidia’s “superchip” really all that super? Are Apple, Intel, AMD, and Qualcomm officially on notice? Have any of us gotten any sleep?Does it just work?Antonio Di Benedetto: Windows on Arm is no longer a wholly subpar experience like it was a few years ago. Thanks in large part to the push around Qualcomm’s Snapdragon X chips, lots of development has been put into native Arm-based apps for Windows. And many x86 apps work fine via Microsoft’s Prism emulation layer.Adobe has had native Arm versions of Photoshop and Premiere for some time now, and even though my precious Lightroom Classic is still an x86-based app I don’t notice any issues using it on Arm. At this point, you’ve gotta be relying on specialized software that’s exclusively x86 based for Windows on Arm to be a non-starter — or you want to freely play any games out there without any worry of incompatibilities.Sean Hollister: Every so often, there’s that moment when an app takes longer to load than it should, and I wonder whether it’ll load at all. Even then, it typically loads. Occasionally, it takes more than one try. My Evernote notes disappeared a few times one day when I alt-tabbed away, but a force refresh fixed that.
paragraph3: And apps don’t seem to respect my system preference for dark mode.But I largely agree with Antonio. I made an RTX Spark my daily driver, with all my typical work and personal apps — Signal, Discord, Audacity, CapCut and Evernote, Irfanview, Slack, ScreenToGif and more — and nothing has failed me so far. I never once needed to think whether I was running an Arm or an x86 app. The real hitches came with gaming and AI, as you’ll read below.Tom Warren: I’ve been using a Windows on Arm laptop with a Qualcomm chip daily for the past two years and things have improved to the point that I can’t tell if an app is native or not anymore. That’s the same story on the RTX Spark laptops, and I feel like Nvidia’s entry into this category will only improve the story for creative apps and gaming.Can it game?TW: Windows on Arm never looked like a serious gaming platform before now. While there still aren’t many native Arm games, Nvidia’s GPU helps bruteforce through the emulation layer. Your mileage in gaming is going to vary depending on the title, but for the most part I’ve found that medium settings, running at 1440p and DLSS performance, will get you to a stable 60fps in most games.I mostly game on my desktop, where I’m spoiled by using an RTX 5090 on a 32-inch 4K screen every day with maxed-out game settings, but I didn’t mind the look of medium settings on a 15-inch display. I was able to run Black Myth: Wukong at 70fps on average at native resolution (3270 x 2180) with medium settings and DLSS performance mode enabled. I ran the same medium settings and DLSS performance in Cyberpunk 2077 and averaged 66fps, and Forza Horizon 6 managed an average of 57fps.
paragraph4: In some titles you may need to drop the resolution or settings lower, though. This definitely isn’t as good as a dedicated gaming laptop, but for something that’s roughly on the level of a MacBook Pro it’s more than good enough for gaming on the go.SH: Like Tom says, the GPU power is there — but the CPU might hold back some of your games. I had plenty of power for a smooth 60fps in Returnal (at 1440p with high settings), Expedition 33 (at a DLSS “Performance” upscaled 1200p with high settings), Jedi Survivor (DLSS “Performance” upscaled 1200p with medium settings), and Shadow of the Tomb Raider (at native 1800p and highest spec).But when I fired up Helldivers 2, even dipping down to a DLSS-upscaled 1080p was no guarantee of 60fps in the highest difficulty missions. There are just too many enemies on screen for the Spark to keep up. Star Wars Zero Company is even more CPU-bound — the Spark didn’t care whether I was maximizing or minimizing the graphics and screen resolution. No matter what I tried, I typically saw my framerate capped between 37fps and 39fps in battle.Even ancient and low-powered games can have quirks. I tried the 2003 title Max Payne 2 and saw situations where framerate dipped to 50fps. I even saw a few hitches in the excellent UFO 50, a collection of 2D games, though a couple other 2D games ran great.I’m also not sure if RTX Spark is suitable for VR yet. The excellent Titanfall 2 VR mod worked, and it seemed to run fine at first, but lost a little stability after a few minutes. That could be my Wi-Fi, because the driver for Valve’s Steam Frame wireless adapter wouldn’t install on the Spark.
paragraph5: Neither did Steam’s streaming audio solution, so the audio came out of the Nvidia laptop instead of the headset.Just so we’re clear, all of this is assuming you want a laptop maxing out its fans and positively dumping heat on your desk or lap. The first night, I set up the Asus ProArt P16, with all 128GB of its ridiculously large pool of memory, and when I booted up Big Walk for my planned online evening with some friends my first thought was, “Well, that looks okay. I guess.” I know Big Walk isn’t some triple-A graphical titan, but it has some fairly demanding graphics for the “friend slop” genre. I expected the N1X to max it out, or at least get close, but not really.
bangla_paragraph1: Nvidia’s RTX Spark N1X processor is finally here, and we’ve been collectively testing a small fortune’s worth of powerful laptops sporting this new “superchip.” RTX Spark is designed to be a high-performing Arm-based SoC for laptops and small desktop computers, rivaling the best from Apple, Intel, AMD, and Qualcomm. It has loads of cores, Nvidia RTX Blackwell graphics, and enough power and unified memory to run sizable local AI models.The flagship placement is inside Microsoft’s Surface Laptop Ultra with a staggering 128GB of unified memory, which our own Tom Warren fully reviewed. Sean Hollister has been testing a 64GB version of the Asus ProArt P16, which I’ve also been testing in its top-spec 128GB config. Since I’m the most spoiled of the lot, I also have a 64GB Lenovo Yoga 9n 2-in-1 and a 32GB HP OmniBook Ultra in for testing.All of these laptops have the same N1X chip with 20 CPU cores and 6,144 GPU CUDA cores, and they’re all wildly expensive — ranging from the HP OmniBook at $3,199.99 to the Asus ProArt’s $6,999.99. There’s an 18-core / 5,120 CUDA N1X chip in lower cost configs, but that only gets as cheap as $2,599.99 for a Surface Laptop Ultra or a smaller Asus ProArt P14 with 24GB of RAM.These are big and expensive laptops built on new chips. They’re meant for developers, coders, and content creators who might also want the ability to use local AI and even play games using the latest Nvidia tech like DLSS 5. There’s a lot to test, and we have not had a ton of time to test it all.
bangla_paragraph2: So below you won’t find an exhaustive scored review of any one laptop, but instead our impressions and thoughts from three writers using five laptops for a week.Is Nvidia’s “superchip” really all that super? Are Apple, Intel, AMD, and Qualcomm officially on notice? Have any of us gotten any sleep?Does it just work?Antonio Di Benedetto: Windows on Arm is no longer a wholly subpar experience like it was a few years ago. Thanks in large part to the push around Qualcomm’s Snapdragon X chips, lots of development has been put into native Arm-based apps for Windows. And many x86 apps work fine via Microsoft’s Prism emulation layer.Adobe has had native Arm versions of Photoshop and Premiere for some time now, and even though my precious Lightroom Classic is still an x86-based app I don’t notice any issues using it on Arm. At this point, you’ve gotta be relying on specialized software that’s exclusively x86 based for Windows on Arm to be a non-starter — or you want to freely play any games out there without any worry of incompatibilities.Sean Hollister: Every so often, there’s that moment when an app takes longer to load than it should, and I wonder whether it’ll load at all. Even then, it typically loads. Occasionally, it takes more than one try. My Evernote notes disappeared a few times one day when I alt-tabbed away, but a force refresh fixed that.
bangla_paragraph3: And apps don’t seem to respect my system preference for dark mode.But I largely agree with Antonio. I made an RTX Spark my daily driver, with all my typical work and personal apps — Signal, Discord, Audacity, CapCut and Evernote, Irfanview, Slack, ScreenToGif and more — and nothing has failed me so far. I never once needed to think whether I was running an Arm or an x86 app. The real hitches came with gaming and AI, as you’ll read below.Tom Warren: I’ve been using a Windows on Arm laptop with a Qualcomm chip daily for the past two years and things have improved to the point that I can’t tell if an app is native or not anymore. That’s the same story on the RTX Spark laptops, and I feel like Nvidia’s entry into this category will only improve the story for creative apps and gaming.Can it game?TW: Windows on Arm never looked like a serious gaming platform before now. Your mileage in gaming is going to vary depending on the title, but for the most part I’ve found that medium settings, running at 1440p and DLSS performance, will get you to a stable 60fps in most games.I mostly game on my desktop, where I’m spoiled by using an RTX 5090 on a 32-inch 4K screen every day with maxed-out game settings, but I didn’t mind the look of medium settings on a 15-inch display. title: Mark Wahlberg on using AI in film ‘the right way’ and being open to an AI clone carrying on his legacy
title_bn: Mark Wahlberg on using AI in film ‘the right way’ and being open to an AI clone carrying on his legacy
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Actor and angel investor Mark Wahlberg says he's OK with using AI in filmmaking, provided it's used "to enhance what you're doing."
paragraph1: Even as Hollywood remains divided over the use of AI in filmmaking, actor and director Mark Wahlberg believes the technology has a place in the industry as long as it’s used the right way. Wahlberg, who’s also an entrepreneur and angel investor, took the stage at TechCrunch Disrupt to share his perspective on AI’s role in filmmaking, and how he’s open to having an AI likeness of himself carry on his legacy. The actor said he plans to potentially use AI to enhance certain aspects of the upcoming Pete Rose biopic, in which he’ll star in the title role. “It’s a fairly expensive movie, but, we’re talking about utilizing [AI] to enhance the stadium setting, things of that nature,” Wahlberg said. “I don’t think you should just, you know, put an idea into ChatGPT and it puts out a script, and then you should go make that and not use real actors.
paragraph2: But if you can use it to enhance what you’re doing, I’m all for that.” That said, Wahlberg made special mention of his belief that storytelling should remain at the heart of filmmaking. Image Credits:Kimberly White/Getty Images for TechCrunch “I’ve done big, effects-driven movies,” Wahlberg said. “I think I was in that kind of sweet spot when the first Jurassic Park was made, or when Perfect Storm came out, and you had that wave, the 100-foot wave that was in the trailer. Those are cutting-edge moments in technology with computer-generated images.
paragraph3: Now, I think it’s hard to do that, so I’m not so passionate about effects-driven movies per se, as opposed to real storytelling.” When asked by TechCrunch Editor-in-Chief Connie Loizos whether he had visited the CAA Vault, a Creative Artists Agency facility which lets actors use scanning technology to capture their bodies, faces, movements, and voices to create AI replicas, Wahlberg said he hadn’t, but would be open to the idea. “I would be interested because I think in the future, if that’s where things go, it would be cool that my children or my grandchildren could be in charge of my likeness and my image, and hopefully put me in some good movies,” Wahlberg said. “It’ll be interesting to see where things go.” He even said he wouldn’t be opposed if his upcoming animated series, “Ted,” continued for decades with an AI version of his likeness.
paragraph4: “I think it’s cool if I’m no longer able to do it or don’t exist, and if it could continue and people want to see it, I think it’d be interesting to see where things go,” Wahlberg said. “I think there’s certain things from my childhood that I wish still existed and were still a part of my life […] I wouldn’t be opposed to it. I think people are going to have massive opportunities to watch whatever it is they want, and if there’s a real audience for that, they should be entitled to have what they want to see.” When you purchase through links in our articles, we may earn a small commission. title: DJ Reinier Zonneveld launches AI music startup GasLab with $1M pre-seed funding
title_bn: DJ Reinier Zonneveld launches AI music startup GasLab with $1M pre-seed funding
author: TechPulse
excerpt: GasLab (Generative AI Solutions Lab), a GenAI music platform created by DJ and producer Reinier Zonneveld, is launched this week, backed by $1 million in pre-seed funding. GasLab is on a mission to k...
paragraph1: GasLab (Generative AI Solutions Lab), a GenAI music platform created by DJ and producer Reinier Zonneveld, is launched this week, backed by $1 million in pre-seed funding. GasLab is on a mission to keep creatives in business in the age of generative AI, protecting the future of the creative industry by ensuring the artists whose music shapes AI-generated tracks are recognised, credited and able to share in the value created. Investors in this round include Eric Demuth, co-founder and executive Chairman of Bitpanda, and Bas Beerens, founder of WeTransfer and serial entrepreneur, alongside other European entrepreneurs. GasLab gives the music industry a complete end-to-end system for AI music. Artists and labels who allow for their music to be used in training its AI model will be able to see exactly how their work helped shape each generated track, and will be paid for it. title: Cult.fit Gets SEBI Clearance For ₹950 Cr+ IPO
title_bn: Cult.fit Gets SEBI Clearance For ₹950 Cr+ IPO
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Markets regulator SEBI has given its go-ahead to gym chain Cult.fit’s ₹950 Cr IPO about three months after it filed…
paragraph1: SUMMARYMarkets regulator SEBI has given its go-ahead to gym chain Cult.fit’s ₹950 Cr IPO about three months after it filed draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) with the regulator As per its DRHP from July, the company’s IPO will comprise a fresh issue of shares worth up to ₹950 Cr and an offer for sale of up to 17.86 Cr shares As per SEBI’s latest processing status, the regulator issued its final observation on the offer documents of Cult.fit on October 12 Markets regulator SEBI has given its go-ahead to gym chain Cult.fit’s ₹950 Cr IPO about three months after it filed draft red herring prospectus (DRHP) with the regulator. As per SEBI’s latest processing status, the regulator issued its final observation on the offer documents of Cult.fit on October 12.
paragraph2: In SEBI parlance, the issuance of final observations signals the regulator’s go-ahead for a company to proceed with its public issue. Cult.fit filed its DRHP in July this year. The company’s IPO will comprise a fresh issue of shares worth up to ₹950 Cr and an offer for sale of up to 17.86 Cr shares. As per sources, The total IPO size is likely to be around ₹4,000 Cr. Early investors like Temasek Holdings, via MacRitchie Investments, Schroders Capital, German fitness operator LifeFit Group, Accel, Tata Digital and cofounder Mukesh Bansal are among the shareholders who plan to offload shares via the OFS.
paragraph3: Cult.fit plans to utilise the funds raised through the fresh issue towards setting up new gym centres, expenditure toward leasing, renting and licensing of existing identified fitness centres, repayment and prepayment of certain borrowings, setting up new exclusive brand outlets, marketing and promotional activities and general corporate purposes. Axis Capital, Goldman Sachs, Jefferies India, JM Financial and Morgan Stanley India are the book running lead managers (BRLMs) to the issue. Founded in 2016, Cult.fit operates a chain of gyms and fitness centres and offers online classes for physical and mental wellbeing. It operated 708 fitness centres across 77 cities in India and had more than ​9.87 Lakh ​paid members as of March 31, 2026.
paragraph4: Out of these, 218 centres are owned and operated by the company. The rest are owned or operated by franchises (288 centres) or by independent owners (202 centres). Cult.fit managed to narrow its net loss for the fiscal year FY26 to ₹251.8 Cr from ₹480.8 Cr in FY25. It posted an operating revenue of ₹1,720.
paragraph5: 6 Cr, up 41.5% from ₹1,215.5 Cr in FY25. The business benefits from a diversified revenue profile, with fitness services contributing roughly 70% of revenues and the fitness products business accounting for the remaining 30%. Cult.fit has raised over $800 Mn to date from investors like Zomato, Accel, Kalaari Capital, Chiratae Ventures, South Park Commons, among others.

title: Snabbit Spent ₹16 To Earn Every Rupee In Operating Revenue In FY26
title_bn: Snabbit Spent ₹16 To Earn Every Rupee In Operating Revenue In FY26
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Amid intense competition in the quick home services market, Snabbit incurred a net loss of ₹167.8 Cr in the financial…
paragraph1: SUMMARYQuick home services startup Snabbit reported a net loss of ₹167.8 Cr in FY26, compared with ₹5.7 Cr in FY25, while operating revenue rose to ₹12.2 Cr from ₹26.3 Lakh Spending on service professionals and customer acquisition far exceeded operating revenue, underscoring the cost of scaling the instant home services business Total expenses stood at ₹194.8 Cr, led by ₹63.1 Cr in service professional costs, ₹48.7 Cr in marketing expenses, and ₹46 Cr in employee benefit expenses Amid intense competition in the quick home services market, Snabbit incurred a net loss of ₹167.8 Cr in the financial year ended March 31, 2026 (FY26) as against a loss of ₹5.7 Cr in FY25. Important to note that FY26 was Snabbit’s first full financial year of operations following its service launch in August 2024. Thus, comparability of the two fiscals is limited. Snabbit posted an operating revenue of ₹12.2 Cr in FY26 compared to ₹26.3 Lakh in FY25.
paragraph2: Platform services generated ₹10.8 Cr in revenue, while uniform sales to service professionals contributed the remaining ₹1.4 Cr. The startup recognises platform service revenue net of discounts it bears. Including other income of ₹14.8 Cr, the startup’s total income for the fiscal stood at ₹27 Cr. Interest on bank deposits contributed ₹14.1 Cr, with the remainder largely coming from gains on mutual fund sales. Snabbit held ₹292.2 Cr in cash and bank balances and ₹26.6 Cr in mutual fund investments, totalling ₹318.9 Cr. This balance predates its $56 Mn Series D funding round in April. Founded in 2024 by former Zepto executive Aayush Agarwal, Snabbit connects users with trained domestic help for cleaning, dishwashing, and other household chores, promising arrivals within 10-15 minutes. The April funding round took the startup’s total funding to $112 Mn.
paragraph3: It is backed by the likes of Susquehanna Venture Capital, Mirae Asset Venture Investments, Bertelsmann India Investments, Nexus Venture Partners, Lightspeed Ventures, among others. Snabbit currently operates in five cities, including Delhi NCR, Mumbai, Bengaluru, Pune and Hyderabad. It intends to expand its operations to 10 cities, with Kolkata and Chennai as priorities. The startup is focusing on penetrating deep into a handful of existing markets, rather than aggressive geographical expansion. Even within cities, it is doubling down on ‘micro-markets’, or certain neighbourhoods where it can ensure quick delivery, rather than the whole city. It was present in 140 micromarkets by May this year, and had onboarded 40,000 professionals on its platforms, with an average order value of ₹169-₹199. Where Did Snabbit Spend In FY26? Snabbit’s total expenses rose to ₹194.8 Cr from ₹6.8 Cr in FY25. Employee Benefit Expenses: These rose to ₹46 Cr from ₹3.3 Cr, including salaries and wages, provident fund contributions, employee stock options, and staff welfare expenses. Expert Service Cost: Its largest expense head stood at ₹63.1 Cr, compared with ₹27 Lakh in FY25. Marketing Expenses: Spending on marketing increased to ₹48.
paragraph4: 7 Cr from ₹82.1 Lakh in the previous year. Service Fulfillment Expenses: Spending under this head stood at ₹23.8 Cr compared with ₹84.5 Lakh in FY25. Snabbit’s Loss Per Job Falls Below ₹200 In a statement issued today, Snabbit’s CEO Agarwal said the startup closed FY26 with a run rate of 35,000 daily jobs, up 70X from around 500 jobs a day at the beginning of the fiscal year. It acquired nearly 10 Lakh customers and onboarded more than 20,000 service professionals during the year. He attributed the growth to investments in customer acquisition, workforce training, technology, infrastructure and geographical expansion. Agarwal said the startup deliberately invested ahead to scale into the competitive quick home services category. The startup said it closed the fiscal with approximately ₹319 Cr in cash and investments, zero borrowings and a net worth of ₹312.4 Cr. He also argued that its annual financial statements do not fully reflect the underlying economics or maturity of the business. In a separate statement, Snabbit claimed that its losses per job declined from approximately ₹1,500 at the beginning of FY26 to below ₹200 in September 2026, indicating an improvement in unit economics as its operations scaled. Its Q2 FY27 metrics show that the platform completed 64.5 Lakh jobs, up 61% QoQ, and recorded a net transaction value (NTV) of ₹73 Cr, up 34%.
paragraph5: House help accounted for 64 Lakh jobs, while more recently launched verticals — home cooking and home salon services — accounted for 50,000 and 10,000 jobs, respectively, in the fiscal. The startup reported an EBITDA loss of ₹145 Cr, equivalent to 199% of NTV. Snabbit also claimed to be the largest high-frequency home services platform by jobs completed and NTV, and the most capital-efficient at the job level. Its strategy centres on building density within fewer cities and micromarkets rather than expanding its geographical footprint aggressively. Competition Heats Up In Quick Home Services Snabbit competes with Pronto and listed home services company Urban Company’s InstaHelp in the instant household assistance market. Pronto closed its $45 Mn Series B round in May at a $200 Mn valuation, adding to the capital flowing into the segment. However, profitability remains a challenge: all three platforms are loss-making due to intense competition, deep discounting, and rising operational costs. Urban Company posted a ₹174 Cr EBITDA loss from InstaHelp in Q2 FY27, over 4X jump from ₹44 Cr in the same quarter last year. InstaHelp fulfilled 6.2 Mn orders, marking a 63% QoQ increase, while its net transaction value (NTV) rose 34% to ₹71 Cr. However, net order value declined to ₹114 from ₹138 in the previous quarter, which it attributed to competitive intensity and introductory pricing for new users. In the past, Urban Company has claimed that it does not expect InstaHelp to meaningfully contribute to its bottom line over the next 4-5 years. The quick home services segment also faces scrutiny over working conditions. Inc42’s reporting documented workers’ concerns about earnings, strict logged-in hour requirements, and inadequate access to waiting areas and washrooms.

Snabbit’s Loss Per Job Falls Below ₹200 In a statement issued today, Snabbit’s CEO Agarwal said the startup closed FY26 with a run rate of 35,000 daily jobs, up 70X from around 500 jobs a day at the beginning of the fiscal year. It acquired nearly 10 Lakh customers and onboarded more than 20,000 service professionals during the year. He attributed the growth to investments in customer acquisition, workforce training, technology, infrastructure and geographical expansion. Agarwal said the startup deliberately invested ahead to scale into the competitive quick home services category. The startup said it closed the fiscal with approximately ₹319 Cr in cash and investments, zero borrowings and a net worth of ₹312.4 Cr. He also argued that its annual financial statements do not fully reflect the underlying economics or maturity of the business. In a separate statement, Snabbit claimed that its losses per job declined from approximately ₹1,500 at the beginning of FY26 to below ₹200 in September 2026, indicating an improvement in unit economics as its operations scaled. Its Q2 FY27 metrics show that the platform completed 64.5 Lakh jobs, up 61% QoQ, and recorded a net transaction value (NTV) of ₹73 Cr, up 34%.
bangla_paragraph5: House help accounted for 64 Lakh jobs, while more recently launched verticals — home cooking and home salon services — accounted for 50,000 and 10,000 jobs, respectively, in the fiscal. The startup reported an EBITDA loss of ₹145 Cr, equivalent to 199% of NTV. Snabbit also claimed to be the largest high-frequency home services platform by jobs completed and NTV, and the most capital-efficient at the job level. Its strategy centres on building density within fewer cities and micromarkets rather than expanding its geographical footprint aggressively. Competition Heats Up In Quick Home Services Snabbit competes with Pronto and listed home services company Urban Company’s InstaHelp in the instant household assistance market. Pronto closed its $45 Mn Series B round in May at a $200 Mn valuation, adding to the capital flowing into the segment. However, profitability remains a challenge: all three platforms are loss-making due to intense competition, deep discounting, and rising operational costs. Urban Company posted a ₹174 Cr EBITDA loss from InstaHelp in Q2 FY27, over 4X jump from ₹44 Cr in the same quarter last year. InstaHelp fulfilled 6.2 Mn orders, marking a 63% QoQ increase, while its net transaction value (NTV) rose 34% to ₹71 Cr. However, net order value declined to ₹114 from ₹138 in the previous quarter, which it attributed to competitive intensity and introductory pricing for new users. In the past, Urban Company has claimed that it does not expect InstaHelp to meaningfully contribute to its bottom line over the next 4-5 years. The quick home services segment also faces scrutiny over working conditions. Inc42’s reporting documented workers’ concerns about earnings, strict logged-in hour requirements, and inadequate access to waiting areas and washrooms.

paragraph5: 8 Cr at the upper end of the price band. Tonbo started off as a subsidiary of a research company, Sarnoff Corporation, providing R&D and technology development services. Since then, the company has pivoted to design and development of advanced imaging and sensor systems used for surveillance, reconnaissance, targeting, and other military applications. Its product portfolio includes thermal imaging systems, weapon sights, fire-control systems, missile seekers, etc. In terms of the value chain, Tonbo handles the prototype development, system integration, and qualification testing in-house, while outsourcing manufacturing to partners such as Kaynes Technology and Avalon Technology. title: Googlebooks are as poorly timed as Valve’s Steam Machine, and may suffer a similar fate
title_bn: Googlebooks are as poorly timed as Valve’s Steam Machine, and may suffer a similar fate
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Google attempted to take its Chromebook platform upscale with Googlebooks. But the timing could not have been worse. Phone support at launch is extremely limited, and most people use Android phones and Chromebooks because they’re cheap.
paragraph1: (Image credit: Tom's Hardware) It’s been a busy year for laptops. Apple’s value-priced MacBook Neo caused a major shakeup in the budget space, forcing Windows device makers to respond with their own premium, affordable offerings.
paragraph2: Microsoft nixed its original 16GB requirement for AI PCs, ushering in a slew of new 8GB Wildcat Lake options, and further muddied the waters of its Copilot branding after vowing to improve performance on 8GB Windows PCs.The driving force behind all of this is, of course, is the roughly five-fold increase in RAM costs in the past year, driven by AI hyperscaler demand.
paragraph3: That’s also why Valve delayed the Steam Machine by roughly six months, eventually forcing its launch price above $1,000. That completely negated the value proposition that made the Steam Deck a success for so long.
