title: The Surface Laptop Ultra delivers on most of Microsoft's promises
title_bn: The Surface Laptop Ultra delivers on most of Microsoft's promises
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Microsoft promises one machine for dev, AI, and gaming, and mostly gets there.
paragraph1: Skip to content Almost there Microsoft promises one machine for dev, AI, and gaming, and mostly gets there. Over the past week, the laptop Microsoft sent me has been summarizing books and movies, generating images from my imagination, and running a 70-billion-parameter AI model that would be a stretch to fit on most laptops. It also played AAA games at a speed and fidelity I would have thought impossible on an ARM system just a year ago. Microsoft wants to sell you one computer for all of your needs, and for once that doesn’t feel like total marketing fluff. Mostly. Microsoft is throwing both arms around the new Nvidia RTX Spark platform with the Surface Laptop Ultra—and setting its sights on the would-be MacBook Pro buyer, or as the company called it, “a high performance audience.” The bet is that rather than a gaming desktop for fun and a development laptop for work, buyers will pay more for one machine that does both. The Surface Laptop Ultra arrives at a strange time in personal computing. Recent industry numbers showed a 20 percent drop in total PC shipments year over year in the third quarter of 2026. That’s not just consumer purchasing either—that’s across the board. Between the RAMpocalypse that has exploded consumer prices and an industry fixated on enterprise money, there hasn’t been much new hardware to excite PC enthusiasts. Microsoft isn’t the only one debuting an RTX-chipped laptop. Dell’s XPS 16 Creator Edition and Asus’s ProArt series (our own Ryan Whitwam‘s review should be appearing on the front page soon) are betting on the chipset as well. The question when reviewing the Surface Laptop Ultra isn’t whether it can achieve the things that it claims competently, but whether there’s finally a compelling reason for power users to switch to an ARM system, and whether their daily workloads can still be achieved without hiccups when compared to a more traditional x86 offering, or the biggest competitor within the segment, the MacBook Pro. With a starting price of $2,599, this is not a budget alternative to Apple silicon.
paragraph2: This is bleeding-edge hardware, and you’re going to be paying a premium for it. Depending on your selected processor and memory options, MSRP can reach as high as $5,899. Prospective buyers should note that the lower-specced 24GB unified memory model ships with Windows 11 Home, while the rest of the fleet arrives with Windows 11 Pro. I received the 64GB model for testing, and I think that would probably be the sweet spot for a lot of users to align cost and performance. I really have to wonder if 24GB is enough to go around when we know that Windows 11 is memory-hungry on its own. When you have to assign a significant portion of that 24GB of unified memory to VRAM for gaming, does performance suffer? An audience question inside the Surface Laptop Ultra review information session asked about the usefulness of the base model, and didn’t get much back other than a vague “useful for smaller models locally” answer. Microsoft may have a more definitive answer to that question a few months from now when software and drivers catch up with hardware. So has the Microsoft and Nvidia team-up created the ultimate all-in-one laptop? Or is this the industry once again putting the hardware hype cart before the finished-software horse? Surface Laptop Ultra specs Specs at a glance: Surface Laptop Ultra Base config As reviewed Screen 3:2, 15-inch mini-LED touchscreen; 3270×2180 (262 PPI) up to 120 Hz dynamic 3:2, 15-inch mini-LED touchscreen; 3270×2180 (262 PPI) up to 120 Hz dynamic OS Windows 11 Home Windows 11 Pro CPU NVIDIA RTX Spark N1X (5120-core GPU, 18-core CPU) NVIDIA RTX Spark N1X (6144-core GPU, 20-core CPU) (4.00 GHz) RAM 24GB LPDDR5x unified memory 64GB LPDDR5x unified memory GPU Blackwell RTX GPU Blackwell RTX GPU Storage 512GB SSD 1TB SSD Networking Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth Core 5.4 Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth Core 5.4 Ports 2 x USB-C/USB4, 1 x USB-C/USB4 w/ Mag Connect, 1 x USB-A 3.1, 1 x HDMI 2.
paragraph3: 1b, SD Card Reader, 3.5mm Headphone Jack 2 x USB-C/USB4, 1 x USB-C/USB4 w/ Mag Connect, 1 x USB-A 3.1, 1 x HDMI 2.1b, SD Card Reader, 3.5mm Headphone Jack Size 12.95×9.40×0.71 inches 12.95×9.40×0.71 inches Weight 4.41 lbs (2.0 kg) 4.41 lbs (2.0 kg) MSRP $2,599.
paragraph4: 99 $4,299.99 Additional features 1080p front-facing webcam 1080p front-facing webcam Tidy internals of the Surface Laptop Ultra. Microsoft promises the laptop is “built with serviceability in mind.” Tidy internals of the Surface Laptop Ultra. Microsoft promises the laptop is “built with serviceability in mind.” Display The 15-inch mini-LED display might not be enough to get folks to run to the Ultra on its own, but it’s a compelling reason to add it to the list. The 3270×2180 native resolution looks simply stunning whether you’re watching a 4K video, playing games, or just staring at a desktop spreadsheet. I preferred the Enhanced color profile, but Vivid and sRGB modes looked fantastic as well. Not the easiest to photograph, but the screen is stunning in person. Not the easiest to photograph, but the screen is stunning in person. Blacks stayed deep against bright, vivid subjects without any sort of visible blooming. I wish I could say the same for my TV. While I can’t quantify how it stacks side by side with the latest MacBook Pro Retina display, I can say that this is a damn nice screen. Viewing angles are superb, colors are punchy, and the 2,000-nit peak brightness kept things legible even in a room flooded with natural sunlight. My only gripe is that in bright rooms, there is glare to contend with.
paragraph5: The glossy glass looks fantastic at lower light levels but can act a bit mirror-like in direct sunlight. It hindered my ability to photograph the screen more than it did my ability to use the computer. Still, if you’re looking for a matte-screen laptop, you might want to keep that in mind. Big Buck Bunny in 4k looks incredible on this screen. Big Buck Bunny in 4k looks incredible on this screen. Keyboard and trackpad The keyboard on the Surface Laptop Ultra is exactly what you’d expect on a premium machine like this. It’s excellent, if unremarkable. The keys have a shallow but satisfying press, the spacing makes sense for my hands, and the whole package delivers a very comfortable typing experience. I don’t have a whole bunch of laptops lying around to compare it to, but unsurprisingly, the closest would be my 2020 MacBook Pro. Microsoft knows what market it’s going after here, and I don’t mind them lifting direct inspiration from Apple in this department. Both the keyboard and the trackpad are excellent. Both the keyboard and the trackpad are excellent. The trackpad is similarly competent. It’s absolutely huge, measuring 5.5 inches long by 3.

I really have to wonder if 24GB is enough to go around when we know that Windows 11 is memory-hungry on its own. When you have to assign a significant portion of that 24GB of unified memory to VRAM for gaming, does performance suffer? An audience question inside the Surface Laptop Ultra review information session asked about the usefulness of the base model, and didn’t get much back other than a vague “useful for smaller models locally” answer. Microsoft may have a more definitive answer to that question a few months from now when software and drivers catch up with hardware. So has the Microsoft and Nvidia team-up created the ultimate all-in-one laptop? Or is this the industry once again putting the hardware hype cart before the finished-software horse? title: Urban Company Board Clears Plans To Raise Up To ₹2,500 Cr
title_bn: Urban Company Board Clears Plans To Raise Up To ₹2,500 Cr
author: TechPulse
excerpt: Urban Company’s board today approved a proposal to raise up to ₹2,500 Cr, alongside approving its financial performance for the…
paragraph1: SUMMARYUrban Company’s board has approved a proposal to raise up to ₹2,500 Cr through issuance of debt or equity The company is seeking funds at a time when InstaHelp is facing tough competition from the likes of Snabbit and Pronto, and the prospect of a cash burn battle It said the fundraise gives it flexibility to invest in its established business lines as well as InstaHelp while pursuing inorganic opportunities, without trading off one for another Urban Company’s board today approved a proposal to raise up to ₹2,500 Cr, alongside approving its financial performance for the September quarter. The proposed funding could involve issuance of equity shares, warrants, fully convertible debentures and convertible preference shares. The fundraise will be executed in one or more tranches via preferential allotment, private placement or one or more qualified institutional placements (QIPs), subject to shareholder approval. The final issue pricing and structure is yet to be determined. “The business is materially larger than at listing, growth has stepped up, and we now operate three businesses at scale with proven economics.
paragraph2: The proposed raise of up to ₹2,500 Cr is about flexibility: it lets us invest with conviction across each of them, cement leadership in InstaHelp, and pursue inorganic opportunities selectively, without trading off one for another,” Urban Company said in a letter to shareholders. The fundraise proposal comes at a time when Urban Company’s quick home services vertical InstaHelp is facing tough competition from the likes of Snabbit and Pronto, resulting in the prospect of a war for market share fuelled by cash burn. Hefty investments in powering the quick home services vertical is also creating a dent in Urban Company’s bottom line. For the September quarter, Urban Company’s net loss more than tripled YoY to ₹182.5 Cr, while operating revenue jumped 41% YoY to ₹537.
paragraph3: 29 Cr. Separately, the board also granted in-principle approval to explore residential air conditioners as a new business category under its product brand Native. This would be subject to further evaluations and final board clearances. “This category represents a large market in which the Company already services millions of units annually, providing it with first-hand insights into the existing product gaps and customer needs,” noted UC’s board. Urban Company made its debut on the bourses just around one year ago.
paragraph4: Hence, its proposed fundraise puts it among the ranks of several new-age tech companies like Kissht, Swiggy, Ather Energy, and Ola Electric that have sought to return to the public markets for fresh capital soon after their IPOs. On a quarterly basis, its net loss nearly doubled from ₹92.1 Cr. Operating revenue remained nearly flat compared with ₹528.3 Cr in Q1 FY27.
paragraph5: The company’s adjusted EBITDA loss for the quarter widened to ₹144 Cr, due to a “deliberate” ₹174 Cr investment in InstaHelp. The company also gave a timeline to improve its bottom line performance in the near future. “We remain on track for Adjusted EBITDA breakeven by Q3 FY28 and Adjusted EBITDA of ₹1,000 Cr by FY31,” it said.
